title: Harappan Sites and Their Features

cards.b: Almost every Prelims paper that touches the Indus civilisation asks which site has what. Learn the sites as a map: what was found, who excavated, which river, which modern state. Over 1,000 sites are known, but about a dozen carry the questions.

Harappa (Punjab, Pakistan, on the Ravi): found by Daya Ram Sahni (1921); granaries, cemetery H, a stone dancing figure. Mohenjodaro (Sindh, on the Indus): R. D. Banerji (1922); the Great Bath, the Granary, the Pashupati seal, the bronze dancing girl. Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat): J. P. Joshi and later R. S. Bisht; Rakhigarhi (Haryana): the largest Indian site; Ganweriwala (Cholistan): unexcavated.

Dholavira lies on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch. It has three divisions (citadel, middle town, lower town) instead of two, huge stepped reservoirs and channels for rain water, and a signboard with ten large letters of the script. UNESCO inscribed it in 2021, India’s first Harappan World Heritage site, as “Dholavira: A Harappan City”.

Lothal (Gujarat, near Bhogavo): S. R. Rao; a brick dock, bead factory, rice husk, a terracotta ship model, fire altars. Chanhudaro (Sindh): bead-making, no citadel; Mackay. Balakot: shell work. Kalibangan (Rajasthan, Ghaggar): ploughed field, fire altars, camel bones, bangles; B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar. Banawali (Haryana): barley, a radial street plan.

Manda (Jammu, on the Chenab) is the northern limit; Alamgirpur (Meerut, UP, on the Hindon) the eastern; Daimabad (Maharashtra, on the Pravara) the southern; Sutkagen Dor (Makran coast, Pakistan) the western. Daimabad has the famous bronze chariot and rhino, though some scholars link it to late Harappan or Jorwe culture.

Surkotada (Kutch): the first actual horse bones, found by J. P. Joshi. Rangpur (Gujarat): rice husk, a Late Harappan site. Ropar (Punjab, Sutlej): the first Harappan site excavated after Independence, a dog buried with a human. Sokhta Koh and Shortughai (Afghanistan): trading posts for lapis lazuli. Sanauli (Baghpat, UP): burials with chariot remains, later than Harappan.

Rakhigarhi’s 2018 to 2019 DNA study of a female skeleton found no steppe ancestry, which supporters use to argue continuity. Many scholars link the dry Ghaggar-Hakra bed to the Vedic Sarasvati; others dispute this. Treat all of it as debated. Mohenjodaro also shows no clear palace, so who ruled remains unknown.

The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) protects sites under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. Dholavira (2021) shows heritage tourism and water-harvesting lessons. A proposed National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal is under development.

• “Match site and discovery” (Lothal: dock; Kalibangan: ploughed field; Surkotada: horse).
  • “Which was the first Harappan site excavated after 1947?” (Ropar).
  • Mains: “Harappan town planning shows a high degree of civic sense. Discuss.” Use grid, drains, three-part Dholavira, dock at Lothal.
  • Always attach river and state.
